title: Installation Jobs Accounts Guidance: Credits, Fee Waivers and Collection
content:
Accounts guidance on credits and fee waivers on **Installation Jobs**, and on how job charges are collected.

## Collection

Job charges are collected with the contract's final balance, so the amount owed on the job is added to the contract balance due. The amount owed on the job is the total of the charges assessed on it less the total of the credits issued on it, over the job's lifetime up to the moment of handling.

## Fee waivers

A fee waiver reverses one specific fee in full and names it as its source. A fee is waived when the job records show it was not owed under these terms, for example:

- a late reschedule fee on a reschedule recorded with enough notice;
- a fee charged twice for the same openings on the same date;
- a lead-safe fee on a home built in or after the stated year.

A fee is waived at most once. The test is whether the job's records already hold a credit naming that same fee as its source.

## Credits for a crew day or a reschedule

A late-arrival credit names the crew day it is for and a company reschedule credit names the reschedule it is for, each granted once.

## Limit

A credit never exceeds the job charges owed; any excess is applied to the contract balance due.

## Points of judgement

| Situation in the job records | Result |
|---|---|
| A fee the records show was not owed, never waived | waived in full, naming that fee |
| The same fee already named by a waiver | not waived again |
| A crew day already credited for late arrival | not credited again |
| A credit larger than the job charges owed | the credit stops at the charges owed; the excess goes to the contract balance due |

*Hypothetical example:* a job owes 120.00 in job charges and is granted a credit of 150.00. The credit reduces the job charges owed to zero, and the remaining 30.00 is applied to the contract balance due.
